topics.title: Definition & Meaning of Charge
explain: Section 2(16) defines a charge as an interest or lien created on a company's property, assets, or undertakings as security for borrowing, including a mortgage.
A Fixed Charge is created on specific, identified, and permanent assets like land, buildings, or heavy machinery.
The company can use fixed charge assets but cannot sell or transfer them without the lender's prior consent.
A Floating Charge is created on fluctuating or changing assets like raw materials, stock-in-trade, or debtors.
The company can freely sell or deal with floating charge assets in its ordinary course of business.

flow.title: Types of Charge on Assets
steps: Fixed Charge locks specific identified assets
Floating Charge covers fluctuating inventory assets

topics.example: Pearl Electronics borrows ₹10 lakh against its office building (Fixed Charge), while Smart Shoes borrows against its leather stock (Floating Charge).
remember: Fixed charge applies to specific identified assets.
Floating charge floats over fluctuating assets like inventory.
mistakes: Thinking a company cannot use fixed charge assets during the loan period—it can use them, but cannot sell them without permission.

quiz.q: Which of the following is defined under Section 2(16) of the Companies Act, 2013?
quiz.why: Section 2(16) specifically defines 'charge' as an interest or lien created on company assets as security, including a mortgage.

quiz.q: What happens to stock-in-trade covered under a floating charge?
o: It can never be sold by the company.
It can be sold in the ordinary course of business.
It requires ROC permission for every sale.
It gets frozen immediately upon borrowing.
quiz.why: Under a floating charge, the company is allowed to deal with and sell assets in its ordinary course of business.

topics.title: Crystallization of a Floating Charge
explain: Crystallization is the legal event where a floating charge converts into a fixed charge on all available assets.
Before crystallization, the floating charge remains dormant, allowing normal business transactions.
It crystallizes when the borrower breaches loan terms, defaults on repayment, ceases business operations, or goes into liquidation.
Once crystallized, the company loses the right to sell or deal with those assets in the ordinary course of business.
The lender can then take control and enforce security on those frozen assets to recover the debt.

flow.title: Process of Crystallization
steps: Borrower defaults or goes into liquidation
Floating charge crystallizes into fixed charge
Assets freeze and company cannot sell stock
Lender enforces security to recover debt

topics.example: Prism Ltd takes a loan against stock; upon default or entering liquidation, the floating charge crystallizes into a fixed charge, freezing the stock.
remember: Crystallization turns a floating charge into a fixed charge.
Occurs on default, cessation of business, or liquidation.
mistakes: Assuming the company can still sell its stock to customers after crystallization has occurred.

quiz.q: When does a floating charge become a fixed charge?
o: When ad valorem fees are paid
quiz.why: Crystallization is the specific event that converts a floating charge into a fixed charge.

quiz.q: Which event does NOT trigger crystallization of a floating charge?
o: Company selling goods in ordinary business
quiz.why: Selling goods in the ordinary course of business is allowed under a floating charge and does not trigger crystallization.

topics.title: Duty to Register Charges & How to Register
explain: It is the statutory duty of the company creating a charge to register its particulars with the Registrar of Companies (ROC).
Registration is required whether the charge is created in India or outside India, on tangible or intangible assets (like patents).
The company must file Form CHG-1 (or Form CHG-9 for debentures) within 30 days of creation along with prescribed fees.
The instrument creating the charge must be signed by both the borrowing company and the charge-holder.
Creating a charge by deposit of title deeds is also compulsorily registrable with the ROC.

flow.title: Registration Process by Company
steps: Prepares instrument signed by both parties

topics.example: Vital Pharmacy creates a charge on its German patents; it must register the charge with ROC India in Form CHG-1 within 30 days.
remember: Normal filing period is 30 days from creation.
Form CHG-1 is used for general charges, CHG-9 for debentures.
mistakes: Thinking intangible assets or assets located outside India are exempt from charge registration.

quiz.q: What is the primary statutory period for registering a charge with the ROC under Section 77(1)?
quiz.why: Section 77(1) mandates that the company must register particulars of the charge within 30 days of its creation.

quiz.q: Which form is used for registration of creation or modification of charge for debentures?
quiz.why: Rule 3 specifies Form CHG-9 for debentures and Form CHG-1 for other charges.

topics.title: Verification of Instrument of Charge
explain: A copy of the instrument creating or modifying a charge filed with the ROC must be properly verified.
If the charged property is situated solely outside India, verification can be done by company seal, signature of a director/CS/lender officer, or an interested third party.
If the property is situated in India (wholly or partly), verification MUST be by a director, company secretary, or an authorized officer of the charge-holder.
Verification by an interested third party is strictly prohibited for properties situated in India.

flow.title: Verification Rules by Asset Location
steps: If in India: verify by Director/CS/Lender Officer
If solely outside India: can also verify by interested third party

topics.example: For a mortgage on land in Mumbai, verification must be done by a company director or CS, not an outside interested party.
remember: Properties in India cannot be verified by an outside interested person.
Solely foreign properties allow verification by an interested person.
mistakes: Allowing an interested third party to verify a charge instrument for property located in India.

quiz.q: Who CANNOT verify a charge instrument if the property is situated in India?
o: An interested person other than company and lender
quiz.why: Third-party interested persons can only verify instruments for properties situated solely outside India.

quiz.q: Under which rule is the verification of charge instrument prescribed?
quiz.why: Rule 3(4) of the Companies (Registration of Charges) Rules, 2014 sets out verification requirements.

topics.title: Extension of Time Limit for Registration
explain: For charges created on or after 02-11-2018, if not registered within 30 days, ROC may allow registration within 60 days of creation on paying additional fees.
If not registered within 60 days, ROC may grant a further 60-day extension (total 120 days from creation) on payment of ad valorem fees.
An application for extension must be made in Form CHG-1/CHG-9 supported by a declaration that it will not prejudice intervening creditors.
For charges created before 02-11-2018, initial extension was up to 300 days, or within 6 months from 02-11-2018 with additional fees.

flow.title: Time Limit Extensions (Post 02-11-2018 Charges)
steps: Register within next 30 days (Days 31-60, Additional fee)
Register within further 60 days (Days 61-120, Ad Valorem fee)

topics.example: A charge created on 16th Feb 2026 can be registered up to 17th April 2026 (60 days) with additional fees to avoid ad valorem fees.
remember: Post 02-11-2018: First 30 days -> Next 30 days (Additional fee) -> Further 60 days (Ad valorem fee).
Maximum ROC extension period is 120 days total from creation.
mistakes: Confusing the additional fee period (days 31-60) with the ad valorem fee period (days 61-120).

quiz.q: For a charge created on 15th March 2026, what is the maximum extended period ROC can grant with ad valorem fee?
quiz.why: Post 02-11-2018 rules allow 30 original + 30 grace + 60 further days = 120 days total from creation.

quiz.q: What type of fee is payable if a charge created in 2026 is registered in the second extension window (days 61 to 120)?
quiz.why: Filing between 61 and 120 days after creation requires payment of ad valorem fees.

topics.title: Deemed Notice of Charge & Certificate
explain: Section 80 establishes that once a charge is registered under Section 77, any person acquiring that property is deemed to have notice of the charge from registration date.
This is a legal fiction called 'Constructive Notice', meaning knowledge is legally implied even if the buyer did not check MCA records.
Upon successful registration, the ROC issues a Certificate of Registration in Form CHG-2 (or Form CHG-3 for modification).
The Certificate of Registration is conclusive evidence that all statutory requirements of Chapter VI have been satisfied.

flow.title: Effect of Registration
steps: Details become public record on MCA portal
All buyers/lenders deemed to have notice

topics.example: Vishnu Marketing registers a building mortgage; Neeraj buys the building later and cannot claim he was unaware of the bank's mortgage.
remember: Deemed notice begins from the date of registration, not creation date.
Form CHG-2 is conclusive evidence of valid registration.
mistakes: Thinking deemed notice starts from the date of creation of charge instead of registration date.

quiz.q: From which date is a person acquiring charged property deemed to have notice of the charge under Section 80?
quiz.why: Section 80 explicitly specifies that deemed notice applies 'from the date of such registration'.

quiz.q: Which form is issued by the ROC as conclusive evidence of fresh registration of charge?
quiz.why: Rule 6 specifies Form CHG-2 for fresh registration of charge and Form CHG-3 for modification.

topics.title: Consequences of Non-Registration of Charge
explain: An unregistered charge is completely void against the liquidator and other creditors during winding up or insolvency.
The lender holding an unregistered charge is reduced to the status of an unsecured creditor at liquidation.
However, the underlying loan contract remains valid, and money can still be recovered through court action against the company.
Failure to register does not absolve the company or officers from criminal penalties under Chapter VI.
A late-registered charge loses priority to any intermediate charge registered earlier.
topics.example: Bank A's charge created June 1 is registered late on Aug 12; Bank B's charge created June 18 is registered June 26. Bank B gets priority over Bank A.
remember: Unregistered charge = Security is void against liquidator & creditors.
Debt obligation remains valid as an unsecured loan.
mistakes: Assuming non-registration makes the loan contract completely void—only the security/charge is void.

quiz.q: If a charge is not registered with the ROC, what is its status against the liquidator during winding up?
quiz.why: Section 77(3) provides that an unregistered charge shall be void against the liquidator and any creditor.

quiz.q: What happens to the borrowing contract if the charge created on property is not registered?
o: The company is released from repaying the debt.
The obligation to repay money secured by charge remains valid.
The money is confiscated by the Central Government.
quiz.why: Section 77(4) states non-registration shall not prejudice any contract or obligation for repayment of money.

topics.title: Application for Registration by Charge-Holder
explain: If the borrowing company fails to register the charge within the initial 30 days, the charge-holder (lender) can apply to the ROC for registration.
Upon receiving the lender's application and instrument, ROC sends a 14-day notice to the company.
If the company does not object or show sufficient cause within 14 days, ROC registers the charge.
The charge-holder is legally entitled to recover all registration fees and additional fees paid to ROC directly from the company.

flow.title: Charge-Holder Registration Process
steps: Company fails to register within 30 days
Lender applies to ROC with instrument

topics.example: A bank files Form CHG-1 when the borrower company neglects to register the loan security within 30 days, then recovers filing fees from the company.
remember: Lender can apply after the initial 30-day company deadline expires.
ROC gives 14 days notice to the company before registering.
mistakes: Thinking the lender can register on day 1 without waiting for the company's 30-day initial period to pass.

quiz.q: How many days notice must the ROC give to the company upon receiving a charge registration application from the charge-holder?
quiz.why: Section 78 specifies that ROC shall give a 14-day notice to the company before allowing registration by charge-holder.

quiz.q: Can a charge-holder recover registration fees paid to ROC from the company?
o: Yes, charge-holder is entitled to recover fees from company.
Only if approved by Central Government.
quiz.why: Section 78 explicitly entitles the charge-holder to recover any fee or additional fee paid from the company.

topics.title: Modification of Charge & Property Acquisition
explain: Section 79 applies Section 77 rules whenever a company acquires property subject to an existing charge, or modifies any existing charge terms.
Modification includes changes in interest rates, loan limits, repayment schedules, or ceding a pari passu charge.
When acquiring charged property, the old charge must be vacated and a new charge registered in the purchasing company's name.
Upon registering a modification, the ROC issues a Certificate of Modification in Form CHG-3.

flow.title: Registration of Charge Modification
steps: Loan terms change or limit enhanced
Company files CHG-1 / CHG-9 for modification

topics.example: OK Bank enhances ABC Ltd's credit facility by ₹20 crore; this limit increase is a modification requiring registration under Section 79.
remember: Any change in terms, limits, or interest rate is a modification.
Certificate of Modification is issued in Form CHG-3.
mistakes: Believing minor loan term changes or limit enhancements do not need ROC registration.

quiz.q: Which of the following events is considered a 'modification of charge' under Section 79?
quiz.why: Enhancing or decreasing loan limits changes the extent/terms of charge and is a modification.

quiz.q: Which certificate is issued by ROC upon registering a modification of charge?
quiz.why: Rule 6 states Certificate of Modification of charge is issued in Form CHG-3.

topics.title: Register of Charges (ROC & Company)
explain: ROC maintains a Register of Charges for every company, open to public inspection on the MCA portal on paying fees.
Every company must maintain a Register of Charges at its registered office in Form CHG-7 containing all charge details.
Copies of instruments creating or modifying charges must also be kept alongside Form CHG-7.
Members and creditors can inspect the company's register without any fee during business hours; others pay prescribed fees.
Form CHG-7 must be preserved permanently, while charge instruments must be kept for 8 years from satisfaction date.

flow.title: Maintenance & Inspection of Register
steps: Enters details forthwith in Form CHG-7
Open for free inspection by members/creditors

topics.example: A shareholder visits the registered office during business hours and inspects Form CHG-7 without paying any fee.
remember: Form CHG-7 register is preserved permanently.
Charge instruments are preserved for 8 years from satisfaction date.
mistakes: Charging inspection fees to existing members or creditors of the company.

quiz.q: In which form must the company maintain its Register of Charges at its registered office?
quiz.why: Rule 10(1) prescribes Form CHG-7 for maintaining the company's Register of Charges.

quiz.q: For how long must instruments creating or modifying a charge be preserved by the company?
quiz.why: Rule 10(4) states charge instruments shall be preserved for 8 years from the date of satisfaction of charge.

topics.title: Company to Report Satisfaction of Charge
explain: When a registered charge is paid off or satisfied in full, the company must intimate ROC in Form CHG-4 within 30 days.
Proviso to Section 82 allows extended intimation up to 300 days from satisfaction date on payment of additional fees.
On receiving CHG-4, ROC sends a show-cause notice to the lender giving up to 14 days to respond, unless CHG-4 is already signed by lender.
If no objection is raised, ROC enters a memorandum of satisfaction and issues Certificate of Satisfaction in Form CHG-5.

flow.title: Satisfaction Reporting Process
steps: Company files Form CHG-4 within 30 days
ROC sends 14-day notice to lender (if CHG-4 unsigned by lender)

topics.example: XYZ Ltd repays its loan in full; it files Form CHG-4 within 30 days, and ROC issues Certificate of Satisfaction in Form CHG-5.
remember: Intimation period: 30 days normally, up to 300 days extended.
Form CHG-4 for filing intimation, Form CHG-5 for ROC Certificate.
mistakes: Thinking ROC sends notice to the lender even if Form CHG-4 is already signed by the charge-holder.

quiz.q: What is the normal time limit for a company to intimate ROC regarding satisfaction of charge?
quiz.why: Section 82(1) mandates intimation of payment or satisfaction within 30 days.

quiz.q: Which certificate is issued by ROC when a memorandum of satisfaction is recorded?
quiz.why: Rule 8(2) provides that ROC issues Certificate of Satisfaction of Charge in Form No. CHG-5.

topics.title: Power of ROC to Enter Satisfaction without Intimation
explain: Section 83 empowers ROC to enter satisfaction or release in the register even if no intimation CHG-4 is received from the company.
Applies when evidence proves debt was paid/satisfied, or property was released or ceased to belong to the company.
This occurs when charged property is sold to a third party and neither company nor lender intimated the ROC.
ROC must inform all affected parties within 30 days of making such entry in the register of charges.
ROC issues Certificate in Form CHG-5 upon full satisfaction recorded under this section.

flow.title: Direct Entry of Satisfaction by ROC
steps: Third party presents proof to ROC
ROC notifies affected parties within 30 days

topics.example: Ranjit buys mortgaged property from PQR Ltd and settles bank dues; he shows proof to ROC, and ROC records satisfaction under Section 83.
remember: ROC can record satisfaction on third-party proof without company intimation.
Affected parties must be notified within 30 days of entry.
mistakes: Thinking only the borrowing company can apply for recording satisfaction of charge.

quiz.q: Under Section 83, within how many days must ROC inform affected parties after making an entry of satisfaction?
quiz.why: Section 83(2) mandates ROC to inform affected parties within 30 days of making the entry.

quiz.q: When does ROC exercise powers under Section 83?
o: When evidence of debt satisfaction is shown even without company intimation
Only on direction of Supreme Court
When company defaults on filing annual return
quiz.why: Section 83 empowers ROC to act on evidence of satisfaction without receiving CHG-4 from company.

topics.title: Intimation of Appointment of Receiver or Manager
explain: If any person obtains a court order or appoints a receiver/manager to manage charged property, they must notify the company and ROC.
The notice must be filed in Form CHG-6 within 30 days of passing the order or making the appointment.
ROC registers the details of receiver, manager, or instrument in the register of charges on payment of fee.
When the receiver or manager ceases to hold office, they must similarly give notice to the company and ROC in Form CHG-6.

flow.title: Receiver Appointment & Cessation Process
steps: Receiver appointed by court or instrument
File Form CHG-6 with ROC within 30 days
ROC enters details in Register of Charges
On cessation, file notice CHG-6 again

topics.example: A bank appoints a receiver to manage a mortgaged factory; the receiver files Form CHG-6 within 30 days with the ROC.
remember: Form CHG-6 is used for both appointment and cessation of receiver.
Time limit for filing notice is 30 days.
mistakes: Failing to file CHG-6 when the receiver or manager ceases to hold appointment.

quiz.q: Which form is used to give notice of appointment or cessation of a receiver/manager under Section 84?
quiz.why: Rule 9 states notice of appointment or cessation of receiver/manager shall be filed in Form CHG-6.

quiz.q: What is the time limit for giving notice of appointment of receiver to the company and ROC?
quiz.why: Section 84 requires notice to be given within 30 days from passing of order or making appointment.

topics.title: Penalties & Rectification by Central Government
explain: Under Section 86(1), a company in default faces a penalty of ₹5,00,000; every officer in default faces a penalty of ₹50,000.
Under Section 86(2), furnishing false/incorrect info or suppressing material facts makes one liable for fraud under Section 447.
Under Section 87, Central Government (Regional Director) can order rectification of register for omissions, misstatements, or delayed satisfaction filings.
Application for rectification is filed in Form CHG-8 if omission was accidental, inadvertent, or didn't prejudice creditors.

flow.title: Central Government Rectification Process
steps: Omission or misstatement in filing occurs
File Form CHG-8 to Central Govt (Regional Director)
CG checks if default was accidental/inadvertent

topics.example: ABC Ltd omitted registering loan modification due to inadvertence; it applies to Regional Director in Form CHG-8 for rectification under Section 87.
remember: Penalty: ₹5 Lakh for company, ₹50,000 for officer in default.
Form CHG-8 is used for CG rectification application under Section 87.
mistakes: Assuming ROC can grant rectification under Section 87—it must be Central Government (Regional Director).

quiz.q: What is the penalty for an officer in default under Section 86(1) for charge non-compliance?
quiz.why: Section 86(1) prescribes a penalty of ₹50,000 for every officer in default.

quiz.q: Which form is filed for seeking rectification of Register of Charges from Central Government under Section 87?
quiz.why: Rule 12 specifies that application for rectification under Section 87 shall be filed in Form CHG-8.
